name: CA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with an 18-point partisan lean
Incumbent Mark DeSaulnier running for reelection with a solid financial advantage
Prediction markets price DeSaulnier at roughly 96% to win
No competitive polling or expert ratings signal a race
model.rationale: DeSaulnier holds a seat that leans Democratic by 18 points, has out-raised Jeff Frese with nearly $590,000 on hand, and markets price his win probability near 96%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting competition, the fundamentals point to a comfortable incumbent victory.
model.watch: Any late surge in outside spending against DeSaulnier or unexpectedly strong Frese fundraising would be the first sign the race is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mark DeSaulnier, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in a Northern California district that voted about 18 points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. He advanced to the general election and enters with a clear financial edge, having raised about $567,000 and holding roughly $586,000 on hand, while Republican Jeff Frese has reported minimal fundraising activity.

No public general-election polling or expert race ratings are available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's resources, and prediction markets, which price DeSaulnier's chances at about 96 percent. The combination of a heavily Democratic electorate, incumbency, and a large money gap makes an upset unlikely, though low-information races always carry some residual uncertainty.
